en: To become less intense or widespread; to decrease
hook: ABATE: the storm takes A BATH and calms down.
story: Abate. To become less intense or widespread; to decrease. All night, the winds of the cyclone howled around Tamara's house near the coast. The tin roof rattled as the family huddled around a lantern. Near dawn, the wind began to abate. By morning the rain had softened to a drizzle, and her father stepped outside. As the storm abated, so did their fear. Abate comes from an old French word meaning to beat down: when a storm abates, its force has been beaten down. So, what verb means for a storm or anger to lessen? ... Abate.

gre.s: The protesters vowed to continue until the government met their demands, so their anger is unlikely to ____ any time soon.
gre.clue: vowed to continue until the government met their demands

example: Once the fever began to abate, Nadia's grandmother finally allowed her to sit up in bed and read.

en: To give extra support to an argument or structure
hook: BUTTRESS: the stone supports holding up a cathedral wall.
story: Buttress. As a noun, a support built against a wall. As a verb, to give extra support to an argument or structure. Andrew's thesis claimed that mangrove forests protect villages from storm surges. His supervisor said the claim was weak. So Andrew spent a month in the coastal mangroves, collecting data from twelve villages, and buttressed his argument with maps and surveys. This time his supervisor nodded. Picture the stone buttresses holding up the walls of an old cathedral; evidence buttresses an argument the same way. So, what verb means to strengthen an argument with support? ... Buttress.

gre.s: Knowing that the jury would distrust a single witness, the lawyer sought to ____ her argument with testimony from three independent experts.
gre.clue: Knowing that the jury would distrust a single witness

example: The researchers buttressed their claim about river pollution with water samples taken from twelve sites along the Buriganga.

en: Causing sudden, violent, and widespread destruction or change
hook: CATACLYSMIC: a CATastrophe, a total CRASH.
story: Cataclysmic. Causing sudden, violent, and widespread destruction or change. Kara's grandfather still speaks quietly about the cyclone of nineteen seventy, which struck the coast of the Bay of Bengal in a single night. Hundreds of thousands of people died, and whole islands were washed clean. It was one of the most cataclysmic storms in recorded history, and it changed the region's politics too. Cataclysm comes from the Greek for a great flood, a washing down. So, what word describes an event of sudden, massive destruction? ... Cataclysmic.

gre.s: Geologists believe that a ____ asteroid impact, which triggered firestorms and years of darkness, wiped out the dinosaurs.
gre.clue: which triggered firestorms and years of darkness

example: Sailors hundreds of miles away heard the cataclysmic eruption of Krakatoa in 1883, which tore the island apart and cooled global weather.

en: To surprise or confuse someone, especially by contradicting expectations
hook: CONFOUND: CONFUSED and DUMBFOUNDED.
story: Confound. To surprise or confuse someone, especially by contradicting expectations. Everyone in Rob's village expected Nina, a shy fisherman's daughter, to leave school after class eight. Instead, she topped the district in her board exams and won a scholarship to study medicine. She confounded every gossip in the market. Even the headmaster admitted that she had confounded his predictions. Confound shares its Latin root with confuse: both mean to pour things together until they are mixed up. So, what verb means to surprise people by proving their expectations wrong? ... Confound.

gre.s: The candidate's landslide victory managed to ____ the pollsters, who had confidently predicted for months that she would lose by a wide margin.
gre.clue: who had confidently predicted for months that she would lose by a wide margin

example: The patient's swift recovery confounded her doctors, who had warned the family to expect several months in hospital.

en: To expose a claim or belief as false
bn: মিথ্যা প্রমাণ করা; ভুল ধরিয়ে দেওয়া
hook: DE-BUNK: removes the BUNK (nonsense).
story: Debunk. To expose a claim or belief as false. A message spread through the family group chat: drinking hot water every fifteen minutes would kill any virus. Jesse's aunt forwarded it to forty people. Jesse, a pharmacy student, looked up the research, found no such evidence, and posted a gentle reply with the facts. Within an hour he had debunked the rumour, and his aunt [chuckle] sent back a sheepish sticker. Bunk is old slang for nonsense, so to debunk is to take the nonsense out. So, what verb means to show that a popular claim is false? ... Debunk.

gre.s: The documentary set out to ____ the popular myth that the ancient monument was built by a lost civilization, presenting overwhelming evidence of its ordinary origins.
gre.clue: presenting overwhelming evidence of its ordinary origins

example: In her first lecture, the physics teacher debunked the idea that heavier objects always fall faster than lighter ones.

en: To force a ruler or leader out of power
hook: DE-POSE: remove from the throne POSITION.
story: Depose. To force a ruler or leader out of power. In seventeen fifty-seven, at the Battle of Plassey, the young ruler of Bengal was betrayed by his own commander. The British East India Company deposed the young ruler and placed the traitor on the throne. Rosie's history teacher said that to depose a ruler is to pull him off his seat of power. Depose comes from Latin words meaning to put down: a deposed leader has been put down from power. So, what verb means to remove a ruler from power? ... Depose.

gre.s: Fearing that the increasingly erratic king would ruin the nation, his generals plotted to ____ him and install his young nephew on the throne.
gre.clue: install his young nephew on the throne

example: In 1688, a group of English nobles invited William of Orange to cross the Channel and help them depose King James II.

en: A close, detailed reading that explains a text, often a sacred one
hook: EXEGESIS: EXPLAINS the text, leading OUT (ex) its meaning.
story: Exegesis. A close, detailed reading that explains a text, often a sacred one. Every Friday evening, Matt's grandfather sat with a few neighbours and explained a single verse of scripture for an hour: the meaning of each word, the history behind it, and what scholars had said over the centuries. His exegesis was so careful that even the young men put their phones away to listen. Ex means out, and the Greek root means to lead: an exegesis leads the meaning out of the text. So, what word means a detailed explanation of a text, especially scripture? ... Exegesis.

gre.s: Her ____ of the poem was so meticulous that it ran to sixty pages, devoting several paragraphs to the possible meanings of a single ambiguous word.
gre.clue: devoting several paragraphs to the possible meanings of a single ambiguous word

example: The legal scholar's exegesis of the constitution's first article filled an entire chapter of her new book.

en: To estimate unknown values by extending known trends
hook: EXTRA-POLATE: extend the line EXTRA far beyond the data.
story: Extrapolate. To estimate unknown values by extending known trends. Shana noticed that the price of onions at the city market had risen by ten cents every week for a month. On a chart, the dots made a neat straight line. She extrapolated the line forward and told her mother to buy a sack before the holiday. Her mother teased her, but two weeks later, the price had climbed exactly as predicted. Extra means beyond: to extrapolate is to extend a pattern beyond the data you have. So, what verb means to predict by extending a trend? ... Extrapolate.

gre.s: Since reliable gauge records existed only up to 1990, the analysts had to ____ from earlier trends to estimate how high the river might be rising today.
gre.clue: Since reliable gauge records existed only up to 1990

example: From melting rates measured over ten summers, the glaciologists extrapolated that the ice shelf could vanish within a century.

en: Occurring by accident rather than design, usually with a happy result
hook: FORTUITOUS: FORTUNE-ate by chance.
story: Fortuitous. Occurring by accident rather than design, usually with a happy result. Blake missed his bus to the coast and had to wait two hours for the next one. On that second bus, he happened to sit beside a manager from a shipping company, and they talked the whole way. A week later he had a job offer. [gasp] It was a fortuitous delay. Fortuitous comes from the Latin fors, meaning chance, the same root as fortune; at its heart, fortuitous means by chance, not by plan. So, what word describes a lucky accident? ... Fortuitous.

gre.s: The discovery of penicillin was largely ____: Fleming noticed the mold only because he had left a dish of bacteria unwashed before going on holiday.
gre.clue: only because he had left a dish of bacteria unwashed

example: The archaeologists made a fortuitous find when a farmer's plough struck a buried terracotta plaque near Mahasthangarh.

en: Fast and energetic in a wild, uncontrolled way
hook: FRENETIC: FRANTIC and FRENZIED.
story: Frenetic. Fast and energetic in a wild, uncontrolled way. Two days before the holiday, Sabrina went shopping at a huge city mall. The place was frenetic: shoppers pushing through doors, salesmen shouting prices, children crying, music blaring from every shop, and escalators packed shoulder to shoulder. [sigh] After three hours, she gave up and bought her dress online. Frenetic is a close cousin of frantic and frenzy, all from the same Greek root. So, what word describes a scene of wild, hurried activity? ... Frenetic.

gre.s: In contrast to the ____ pace of the trading floor, where brokers shouted orders and rushed between screens, the bank's research department was quiet and contemplative.
gre.clue: brokers shouted orders and rushed between screens

example: The final week before the science fair was frenetic, with students soldering wires and rewriting posters until midnight.

en: An embarrassing social mistake
hook: GAFFE: a GAFFE makes everyone LAUGH at you.
story: Gaffe. An embarrassing social mistake. At her fiancé's family dinner, Heidi tasted the biryani and said brightly, "This is wonderful! Which restaurant did you order it from?" The table went silent. His mother had spent all day cooking it. [gasp] Heidi's cheeks burned, but his grandmother [laugh] patted her hand, and soon everyone was smiling. Heidi still remembers that gaffe. Gaffe rhymes with laugh, and a gaffe is a slip that makes people laugh at you. So, what word means an embarrassing social blunder? ... Gaffe.

gre.s: The ambassador's ____ was mocked for weeks: at a state dinner, he raised his glass to the host country using the name of its bitter rival.
gre.clue: he raised his glass to the host country using the name of its bitter rival

example: Forgetting the bride's name halfway through his wedding speech was a gaffe that Rafi's friends never let him forget.

en: To provoke or urge someone into action
hook: GOAD: a pointed stick used to push cattle forward.
story: Goad. As a noun, a pointed stick for driving cattle. As a verb, to provoke or urge someone into action. In the village of Zeke's childhood, farmers walked behind their oxen with a thin bamboo goad, tapping the animals forward through the mud. Years later, at university, his friends goaded him into entering a debate competition he was too shy to try. He won second place. To goad someone is to give them a little poke, like the farmer's stick. So, what verb means to provoke or prod someone into acting? ... Goad.

gre.s: Hoping to ____ the prime minister into calling an early election, the opposition filled parliament with taunts, but she refused to be provoked.
gre.clue: the opposition filled parliament with taunts

example: The older boys goaded Tanvir into jumping from the high diving board, even though he could barely swim.

en: Arrogantly superior and disdainful
hook: HAUGHTY: HIGH and mighty, nose in the air.
story: Haughty. Arrogantly superior and disdainful. At the wedding reception, Amelia's distant cousin arrived from London in sunglasses, looked around the community centre, and announced that the food back home was much better. She refused to sit near the children and spoke to the waiters without looking at them. Her haughty manner left a chill at every table. Haughty comes from the French haut, meaning high: a haughty person holds her nose high. So, what word describes someone proud who looks down on others? ... Haughty.

gre.s: The heiress was so ____ that she refused even to acknowledge the servants, addressing them only through her secretary as though they were beneath her notice.
gre.clue: as though they were beneath her notice

example: The haughty critic dismissed every film at the festival as amateurish without bothering to watch more than ten minutes of any.

en: Arrogantly commanding; expecting to be obeyed
hook: IMPERIOUS: like an EMPEROR giving orders.
story: Imperious. Arrogantly commanding; expecting to be obeyed. When the new factory manager arrived at the plant, he snapped his fingers at workers, demanded tea without ever saying please, and never learned anyone's name. "Do it now" was his favourite sentence. Barry, a supervisor of twenty years, found his imperious tone hard to bear. Imperious shares a root with empire and emperor: an imperious person gives orders like an emperor. So, what word describes someone who orders others around as if they were royalty? ... Imperious.

gre.s: The duchess dismissed the servants with an ____ wave of her hand, never deigning to look at them.
gre.clue: never deigning to look at them

example: The new manager's imperious emails, full of commands and deadlines but never a single please, soon drove two engineers to resign.

en: Having or showing good judgment
hook: JUDICIOUS: like a wise JUDGE.
story: Judicious. Having or showing good judgment. When Nicole's family argued about whether to sell their land in the village or keep it, voices rose and tempers flared. Nicole's mother listened quietly to everyone. Then she suggested selling half and keeping half, so the family could pay its debts and still keep a home to return to. One by one, everyone agreed. It was a judicious decision. Judicious is linked to judge: a judicious person weighs things like a wise judge. So, what word means showing wise and careful judgment? ... Judicious.

gre.s: With only limited funds available, the museum made a ____ decision to repair its roof before purchasing any new artworks.
gre.clue: repair its roof before purchasing any new artworks

example: A judicious use of colour, just one red chair in an otherwise grey room, made the small apartment feel striking.

en: Worthy of praise and admiration
hook: LAUD = praise, as in applaud.
story: Laudable. Worthy of praise and admiration. Every Friday, Ross, a small-town college student, spends his only day off teaching street children to read under a tree near the railway station. He buys the chalk and notebooks with his own pocket money. When a local newspaper wrote about him, it called his effort laudable, and three more volunteers joined him the next week. To laud means to praise, so laudable means worthy of praise; on diplomas, cum laude means with praise. So, what word describes an action that deserves praise? ... Laudable.

gre.s: Although the program's goals were ____, its execution was so poor that it ultimately did more harm than good.
gre.clue: its execution was so poor

example: The club's laudable plan to plant a tree for every goal scored this season has already greened three school playgrounds.

en: Flashy and meant to show off wealth or importance
hook: OSTENTATIOUS: 'OSTEN-TATIOUS', 'Look at me, look at my stuff!'
story: Ostentatious. Flashy and meant to show off wealth or importance. When a businessman's son got married in the city, the guests arrived to find a line of white cars, a chocolate fountain, and a stage covered in thousands of imported roses. The groom rode in on a decorated horse, followed by a brass band. Mandy whispered to her friend that it was all rather ostentatious. Ostentatious comes from the Latin for showing off, and ostentatious things seem to shout, look at me. So, what word describes a display that is flashy and showy? ... Ostentatious.

gre.s: Though enormously wealthy, the philanthropist lived without ____ display, driving an old car and living in a modest house.
gre.clue: driving an old car and living in a modest house

example: The minister's ostentatious motorcade of twenty cars jammed Mirpur Road for an hour during the morning rush.

en: Flamboyant confidence and stylish flair
hook: PANACHE: originally a feather plume on a knight's helmet. Pure style.
story: Panache. Flamboyant confidence and stylish flair. At the university cultural night, Adam walked onto the stage in a bright yellow suit, bowed with a sweep of his arm, and sang an old folk song as if the whole auditorium belonged to him. He even winked at the front row. [laugh] The students cheered for five minutes. He sang with real panache. Panache was once the feather plume on a knight's helmet; a person with panache wears confidence like that bright plume. So, what word means confident, stylish flair? ... Panache.

gre.s: The chef plated each dish with such ____, flambéing desserts at the table with a theatrical flourish, that diners often applauded.
gre.clue: with a theatrical flourish

example: The goalkeeper saved the last penalty with real panache, diving full length and springing up at once to salute the crowd.

en: Overly concerned with minor details or rules; showing off learning
bn: পাণ্ডিত্য জাহির করে এমন; খুঁটিনাটি নিয়ে অতিরিক্ত মাথাব্যথা
hook: PEDANTIC: a PEDAL-pushing professor who corrects every tiny thing.
story: Pedantic. Overly concerned with minor details or rules; showing off learning. When Chelsea told a story about her trip to the hills, her cousin kept interrupting. "Actually, it was not three hours, it was two hours and fifty minutes." "Actually, that hill is not a mountain." [sigh] By the end, nobody wanted to hear about the trip. His pedantic corrections had killed the story. A pedant was once a schoolmaster, and a pedantic person still corrects everyone like a fussy teacher. So, what word describes someone obsessed with tiny details? ... Pedantic.

gre.s: Students found the lecturer ____, as he would interrupt a lively discussion to correct a trivial grammatical error.
gre.clue: interrupt a lively discussion to correct a trivial grammatical error

example: The editor's pedantic notes on comma placement filled the margins, yet she said nothing about the plot's glaring holes.

en: Having knowledge of events before they happen
bn: দূরদর্শী; ভবিষ্যৎ আগে থেকে জানে এমন
hook: PRE-SCIENT: knowing (scient, science) beforehand.
story: Prescient. Having knowledge of events before they happen. One April, Sam's grandmother watched the sky and the ants carrying food up the walls and said, "The floods will come early this year. Move the rice up to the loft." Everyone smiled at her. In June, the water rose weeks early, and theirs was the only rice in the village that stayed dry. Her warning had been prescient. Pre means before and scient means knowing, as in science: prescient means knowing beforehand. So, what word describes someone who foresees the future accurately? ... Prescient.

gre.s: The novel now seems remarkably ____, having described smartphones and social media decades before either existed.
gre.clue: decades before either existed

example: In 1965, Gordon Moore made the prescient forecast that the number of transistors on a chip would keep doubling.

en: To argue about trivial matters; a minor objection
hook: QUIBBLE: a small QUIBBLE, like a QUIBBLING nibble.
story: Quibble. To argue about trivial matters; also, a minor objection. Bella and her brother had planned a family trip to the hills for weeks. But on the night before, they spent an hour quibbling over who would sit by the window on the train. [chuckle] Their father finally said, "You will take turns. One more quibble and we all stay home." Silence fell at once. Quibble rhymes with nibble: small nibbles at an argument instead of a real bite. So, what verb means to argue over small, unimportant things? ... Quibble.

gre.s: The reviewer admired the novel's ambition and its vivid characters; her only ____ concerned a handful of typographical errors that hardly diminished its power.
gre.clue: that hardly diminished its power

example: The two professors quibbled for an hour over whether the manuscript dated from 1802 or 1803.

en: To deliberately dodge work or a duty you should do
hook: SHIRK: like a SHARK swimming away from work.
story: Shirk. To deliberately dodge work or a duty you should do. Toby was part of a group project on river pollution. While his three teammates collected water samples from the city river in the heat, he always had an excuse: a headache, a cousin's wedding, a broken phone. On presentation day, he tried to take the credit. The teacher, who had seen everything, gave him a lower mark for shirking his duties. Shirk sounds like shark: picture a lazy shark slipping away whenever there is work to do. So, what verb means to dodge a responsibility? ... Shirk.

gre.s: Unlike her predecessor, who tended to ____ difficult decisions by delegating them to committees, the new director confronted every problem personally.
gre.clue: by delegating them to committees

example: Soldiers who shirked guard duty during the campaign were ordered to dig latrines for a week as punishment.

en: To replace something older or less effective
hook: SUPER-SEDE: sits (sede) above, takes the top seat.
story: Supersede. To replace something older or less effective. Mia's grandfather kept a heavy black telephone with a turning dial on his desk for thirty years. When the family gave him a smartphone, he grumbled at first, then discovered video calls with his granddaughter in Canada. [laugh] The new phone soon superseded the old one, though he kept it on his desk for memory's sake. Super means above and sede means sit: whatever supersedes the old thing takes the higher seat. So, what verb means to replace something older? ... Supersede.

gre.s: Most experts expect electric vehicles to eventually ____ gasoline-powered cars, just as cars once replaced horse-drawn carriages.
gre.clue: just as cars once replaced horse-drawn carriages

example: The 2024 building code supersedes all earlier guidelines, so builders in Chattogram must now follow its stricter fire rules.

en: To cheat someone out of money; a fraud
hook: SWINDLE: like a WINDOW that's actually a painting, a trick.
story: Swindle. To cheat someone out of money; a fraud. A man knocked on Shane's grandmother's door, claiming he could double her savings in a month through a special scheme. He showed shiny papers and an official-looking card. Luckily, Shane arrived, checked the man's name online, and found he had already swindled twenty families in the town. The police were called. Swindle sounds like dwindle: when someone swindles you, your money dwindles to nothing. So, what verb means to cheat someone out of money? ... Swindle.

gre.s: The so-called investment firm existed only to ____ elderly retirees, promising guaranteed returns before disappearing with their life savings.
gre.clue: disappearing with their life savings

example: Online scammers swindled a retired schoolteacher in Rajshahi by posing as bank officers and asking for her PIN.

en: Using few words; abrupt
hook: TERSE: TERSE is a terse word, just five letters.
story: Terse. Using few words; abrupt. Dina sent her boss a long, careful email explaining why the report would be two days late, with three apologies and a new plan. His reply came back in one word: "Fine." She stared at it for a full minute, unsure whether he was angry. [chuckle] Later she learned that every email he wrote was that terse. Terse once meant wiped clean and polished; a terse reply is wiped clean of every extra word. So, what word describes a reply that is short and curt? ... Terse.

gre.s: Expecting a warm thank-you for her months of work, the volunteer was stung by the director's ____ reply, which consisted of a single, unsigned line.
gre.clue: which consisted of a single, unsigned line

example: Asked about the defeat, the coach gave a terse answer, 'We played badly,' and walked straight out of the press room.

en: Not permanent; lasting a short time
hook: TRANSITORY: in TRANSIT, passing through.
story: Transitory. Not permanent; lasting a short time. Every spring, the silk cotton trees along Morgan's village road burst into red blossoms. For two weeks the road looks as if it is on fire, and children collect the fallen flowers in their laps. Then the petals drop, and the trees turn plain and green again. His mother says beauty is always transitory. Transitory is related to transit: something transitory is just passing through. So, what word describes something brief and temporary? ... Transitory.

gre.s: The economic boom proved ____: within two years, the new factories had closed and unemployment had returned to its former levels.
gre.clue: within two years, the new factories had closed

example: Fame on social media is often transitory, as last month's viral singer from Khulna has already discovered.

en: Unimportant or trivial
hook: TRIFLE: a small, unimportant thing.
story: Trifling. Unimportant or trivial. Two brothers in Paula's neighbourhood stopped speaking for a year over a trifling matter: who had broken a plastic chair at a family picnic. The chair cost five dollars. When their mother finally sat them down, both were embarrassed by how trifling it seemed. [laugh] They bought a new chair together that same afternoon. A trifle is a small thing of little value, and trifling describes anything that small. So, what word describes a matter too minor to fight over? ... Trifling.

gre.s: Although the fine was ____, a mere ten dollars, the principle at stake led the activist to appeal all the way to the supreme court.
gre.clue: a mere ten dollars

example: Compared with the cost of rebuilding the bridge, the repair bill seemed trifling, so the council approved it at once.

en: Not proper or appropriate; in bad taste
hook: UN-SEEMLY: doesn't SEEM right.
story: Unseemly. Not proper or appropriate; in bad taste. At a quiet prayer gathering after a neighbour's death, Tristan was shocked to see two guests arguing loudly about a land deal in the courtyard. Heads turned, the women inside fell silent, and an elder walked over to stop them. Shouting about money at such a time was deeply unseemly. Seemly is an old word for fitting and proper, so unseemly means not fitting the occasion. So, what word describes behaviour that is improper for the occasion? ... Unseemly.

gre.s: Many guests found the candidate's lavish victory party ____, since it took place just hours after deadly floods had devastated the region.
gre.clue: just hours after deadly floods had devastated the region

example: Cheering loudly in the hospital corridor seemed unseemly to the nurses, even though the family had just heard good news.

en: Lively and full of energy, especially in personality
hook: VIVACIOUS: full of VIVA (life).
story: Vivacious. Lively and full of energy, especially in personality. When Nadia joined the office, the quiet floor changed almost overnight. She learned everyone's name in a day, brought homemade cookies on Thursdays, and laughed so brightly that even the stern accountant smiled. Her vivacious spirit made Mondays bearable. Vivacious comes from the Latin vivere, to live, as in vivid and survive: a vivacious person is full of life. So, what word describes someone lively and spirited? ... Vivacious.

gre.s: Unlike her reserved older sister, Shathi was ____, filling every room with laughter and chatter from the moment she arrived.
gre.clue: Unlike her reserved older sister

example: The vivacious tour guide kept forty tired schoolchildren laughing all the way around Lalbagh Fort.

en: Full of sorrow; very bad or deplorable
hook: WOEFUL: full of WOE.
story: Woeful. Full of sorrow; very bad or deplorable. Kirk's college cricket team had practised for months, but in the final they were all out for thirty-one runs in just ten overs. The coach called it a woeful performance. Kirk himself looked woeful all evening, kicking stones on the long walk home while his friends stayed silent. Woeful simply means full of woe, and woe is deep sorrow. So, what word describes a performance that is shockingly bad? ... Woeful.

gre.s: Although the school boasted of its modern facilities, inspectors found its science laboratories in ____ condition, with broken equipment and no working gas supply.
gre.clue: with broken equipment and no working gas supply

example: The team's woeful defending allowed their opponents to score four goals in the first half alone.
